summary.text: Warren Davidson is the Republican incumbent in Ohio's 8th District, a seat he has held since winning a 2016 special election to succeed John Boehner. A West Point graduate and former Army infantry officer, he spent about 15 years in Ohio manufacturing before entering Congress. He chairs the National Security and Illicit Finance subcommittee of the Financial Services Committee and also serves on the Foreign Affairs Committee.

paragraphs.text: Davidson was born and raised in Sidney, Ohio, and graduated from Sidney High School in 1988.
He enlisted in the Army after high school, then earned an appointment to West Point and graduated in 1995 with a degree in American history.
He served as an infantry officer in the Old Guard, the 75th Ranger Regiment and the 101st Airborne Division before leaving the Army in 2000.

After the Army, Davidson earned an MBA from the University of Notre Dame and spent 15 years starting, acquiring and growing manufacturing companies in Ohio, according to his House website. Wikipedia reports that he bought his father's business, West Troy Tool & Machine, in 2005 and combined it with another firm in 2014.
He served on the Concord Township, Ohio, Board of Trustees from 2004 to 2005 and chaired the Dayton Region Manufacturers Association.

Davidson won a 15-way Republican primary and the June 7, 2016 special election to fill the remainder of former Speaker John Boehner's term, and was sworn in on June 9, 2016. He has been elected to full terms since, including over Democrat Vanessa Enoch in 2018, 2020 and 2022.
He founded the Sound Money Caucus in July 2020 and chairs it, and he was policy chair of the House Freedom Caucus from October 2019 until July 2024.
In the 119th Congress he serves on the Financial Services Committee, where he chairs the National Security and Illicit Finance subcommittee, and on the Foreign Affairs Committee.
According to his House website, he and his wife Lisa have been married for 30 years and have two adult children.
